figure_description: A Cartesian coordinate grid of equal square units. The horizontal axis is labeled x with an arrow to the right, and the vertical axis is labeled y with an arrow pointing upward. The origin is labeled 0. On the x-axis, grid lines are marked with tick marks at -1 (one grid unit to the left of the y-axis) and 1 (one grid unit to the right of the y-axis). On the y-axis, the grid line one unit above the x-axis is labeled 1. The grid extends from x = -3 to x = 3 horizontally, and from y = 0 to y = 5 vertically. A straight line labeled l with arrows at both ends passes through the grid, intersecting the horizontal axis at the grid line x = -2 (at the point (-2, 0)) and passing through the grid intersection at x = 3, y = 2 (three units right of the y-axis and two units above the x-axis).
